reasons: Direction is correct for our side: Corio is the customer/licensee and Commerce One the vendor/licensor, and the edit adds vendor-side obligations without creating or broadening any Corio indemnity.

The rationale accurately reads the source: Section 8.1 already contains a vendor third-party IP infringement indemnity with notice/control/cooperation mechanics and procure-modify-replace-refund remedies, and no offsetting customer indemnity exists, so the remaining gap is the non-IP heads (breach of law, data breach caused by vendor, gross negligence/wilful misconduct).

Redline is minimal and surgical: new Section 8.3 tracks the playbook model language, expressly limits itself to third-party claims 'to the extent resulting from' the added heads, incorporates the Section 8.1 procedure by reference, and leaves the existing 8.1 remedy structure and 8.2 infringement exclusions untouched.

The failed deterministic check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a false negative of the heuristic: the IP limb sits in unchanged paragraph p0086 (Section 8.1) rather than in the inserted text, so no IP cover was lost.

Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook position, and offers a sensible fallback (capping only the additional heads, not the IP indemnity), which is consistent with the fallback tier.

Severity should be reduced: the critical limb (vendor IP indemnity, standard procedure, no one-way customer indemnity) is already satisfied, so the residual gap in ancillary indemnity heads is a medium-severity issue rather than critical.
